cohort: 367 newborns in government hospitals of the Eastern Amhara region, Northeastern Ethiopia
finding: The prevalence of birth asphyxia was 13.1%, with significant predictors including maternal illiteracy, low birth weight, primiparity, preterm birth, and cesarean section delivery.
mod_finding: Cesarean section delivery was associated with an increased risk of birth asphyxia.
gest_age: Preterm birth (<37 weeks) was a significant predictor of birth asphyxia.
birth_weight: Low birth weight was a significant predictor of birth asphyxia.
